targets.rationale: Both Tools prevent 60 attack damage once and are then discarded. Changing the protected attacker type from Metal to Psychic preserves the full mechanic and numbers but materially shifts matchup coverage.

Both Tools prevent 60 attack damage once and are then discarded. Changing the protected attacker type from Metal to Dragon preserves the full mechanic and numbers but materially shifts matchup coverage.

Both Supporters draw until the user has 6 cards in hand. Iris's Fighting Spirit requires discarding another card as a play cost, which preserves the draw-to-six effect but materially worsens its card economy and playability.

Both symmetric Stadiums place 2 damage counters on Basic Pokemon while exempting one type. The different trigger and exempted type materially change when and where the damage applies, but preserve the same disruptive role.

Both Tools reduce attack damage to the attached Pokemon. The reduction changes from 40 while behind on Prizes to 30 against attackers with Abilities, which preserves the defensive role but materially changes its activation condition.
Both Items can gust an opposing Benched Pokemon. The target is coin-dependent and removes Double Gust's forced switch on the user's side, creating a major reliability and board-state difference.

The target preserves species, stage, type, Weakness, Retreat Cost, and the 30-damage evolution-line role. Losing 10 HP and replacing the source's draw attack with damage is a material utility difference.
The target preserves species, stage, type, HP, Weakness, Retreat Cost, and an inexpensive 30-damage attack. It loses the draw option and incurs self-damage, materially reducing flexibility.
Both Items search one Energy into the hand. Searching the whole deck but only for Basic Energy replaces a top-7 search that may take Special Energy, materially changing reliability and coverage.

Both Items discard Energy from an opponent's Pokémon without a coin flip or other play condition. Enhanced Hammer is limited to Special Energy rather than any Energy, materially narrowing targets while retaining direct Energy denial.

Both Supporters draw a number of cards scaled by the opponent's Pokémon in play. Morty's Conviction counts only the Bench and requires a discard, whereas Erika's Hospitality also counts the Active and instead requires a hand of 5 or fewer including itself, changing cost and ceiling but retaining opponent-board-scaled draw.

Both Tools always reduce the attached Pokémon's Retreat Cost by 1 Colorless. Rescue Board replaces permission to retreat while Asleep or Paralyzed with free retreat at 30 HP or less, so the baseline mobility is shared but the situational benefit differs.

Both unrestricted Items choose and discard up to 2 Pokémon Tools from either player's board. Tool Scrapper lacks Field Blower's additional Stadium-removal choice, so the Tool-removal mode is retained but the source's broader board control is not.

Both Items inspect exactly 7 deck cards, optionally take 1 Pokémon, and shuffle the remainder back. Dusk Ball inspects the bottom rather than the top, a narrow but real difference when deck order is known or manipulated.

Both Items fill the opposing gust role. Replacing a guaranteed GX/EX-only gust with an unrestricted coin-flip gust removes the discard cost but materially changes reliability and target coverage.

Both unrestricted Supporters force a chosen opposing Benched Pokémon into the Active Spot. Boss's Orders omits Guzma's mandatory follow-up switch of the user's own Active Pokémon, preserving gust control while losing the coupled pivot.

Both are unrestricted Supporters that replace both players' hands and redraw for both players, preserving Iono's core hand-reset and disruption role. Judge instead shuffles into the deck and always draws four, so it loses Prize-count scaling and materially changes late-game effectiveness.

Both are unrestricted Supporters that put both players' shuffled hands on the bottom of their decks before both players redraw. Lucian replaces deterministic Prize-count scaling with independent coin flips for three or six cards, materially changing reliability and comeback disruption.

Both are unrestricted Supporters that reset and redraw both players' hands, including potentially asymmetric hand sizes. Harlequin shuffles the hands into the decks and uses one coin flip for a five-three split rather than each player's remaining Prize count, materially changing control and timing.

Both Items unconditionally remove 1 Special Energy attached to an opponent's Pokémon. Enhanced Hammer discards it rather than sending it to the Lost Zone, retaining the immediate denial but allowing later discard recovery.
Both Tools increase attack damage to the opposing Active Pokémon. Brave Bangle gives 30 rather than 20 damage but is restricted to Rule-Box-free attackers hitting Pokémon ex.

Both standalone Colorless Basic Pokémon can fill an early-game hand-refresh slot. Audino costs one Energy, draws only up to six, lacks sleep protection and free retreat, and has much higher HP, so this is only a low-confidence role substitution.

Both ordinary Psychic Basic Pokémon have the same search-for-two-Basic-Energy attack effect. Gimmighoul requires one Energy instead of attacking for free and differs substantially in HP, retreat, and its additional attack.

Both Supporters inspect a hidden opponent zone and discard Item cards. Eri acts on the hand with a two-Item cap rather than the top five deck cards, so the disruption role is preserved with a material targeting difference.

Both Items accelerate Basic Energy from the deck onto a Pokémon. Energy Coin removes the Prize and Ultra Beast restrictions but attaches only one Energy and succeeds on only a double-heads flip, a major effectiveness difference.
Both Items make the opponent switch their Active Pokémon and let the opponent choose the replacement. Repel materially differs by not also switching the user's Active Pokémon.

Both Items attempt to accelerate one Basic Energy from the deck to a Pokémon. Their success condition and eligible targets differ materially: a double-heads full-deck search versus the top six cards and a Benched Basic Pokémon.
Both Colorless Basic Pokémon offer a one-Energy hand-refill attack. Audino draws to six rather than shuffling and drawing seven, lacks Cleffa's Baby Rule and free retreat, and has much higher HP.

Both Items put cards from the user's deck into the discard pile. Hole-Digging Shovel is a substantially weaker substitute because it mills two unknown top cards instead of selecting up to three cards.
Both Supporters shuffle the user's hand into the deck and draw a replacement hand. Lacey draws four or conditionally eight rather than the prior hand size plus one.
Both Supporters shuffle the user's hand into the deck and draw a replacement hand. Lillie's Determination draws six or conditionally eight rather than the prior hand size plus one.
Both Items search Basic Energy from the deck into the hand. Energy Search retrieves one Energy without a discard cost instead of up to four Fire Energy after discarding two cards.

Both Supporters provide early Pokémon setup by searching for Basic Pokémon. Brock's Scouting finds fewer Basics and puts them into the hand rather than directly onto the Bench, a major tempo difference.

Both Supporters put both players' hands on the bottom of their decks and redraw for both players. Lucian replaces Marnie's deterministic 5-card user and 4-card opponent hands with independent coin flips for 3 or 6, materially changing reliability and disruption.

Both Items heal 1 of the user's Pokémon and require discarding Energy from that Pokémon. Super Potion caps healing at 60 and discards 1 Energy, while Max Potion heals all damage and discards all attached Energy, preserving the healing-for-Energy tradeoff with materially different scale.

Both cards are 70-HP single-prize Metal Basic Beldum with matching Weakness, Resistance, and Retreat Cost, and both retain a one-Metal 10-damage attack. The target's other attack costs an additional Colorless Energy, deals 30 more damage, and causes 10 self-damage, which is a material effectiveness change within the same deck slot.

Both Supporters draw two cards and add an upside under a condition. The target can draw two more cards when the hand is large instead of recycling itself when Community Center is in play, retaining the core draw mechanic with a different secondary effect.
Both are generic draw Supporters. Cheren draws one additional card but lacks Caretaker's conditional self-recycling effect, a modest numerical and secondary-effect difference.

Both Pokémon Tools primarily improve mobility by reducing Retreat Cost. Air Balloon applies to any Pokémon but reduces the cost by two rather than guaranteeing free retreat for Future Pokémon, and it omits the source's 20-damage bonus, so it preserves only the broad strategic slot.

Both Items search for low-HP Pokémon without a discard cost. Buddy-Buddy Poffin can find two cards but requires Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or less and benches them directly, rather than finding one Pokémon with 90 HP or less and putting it into the hand.

Both Items search the deck for a Pokémon and put it into the hand. Ultra Ball removes the HP restriction but requires two cards to be discarded, a material resource-cost difference while preserving the search role.

The target keeps the evolution family coherent but replaces the source's attack-focused and defensive effects with Metal Energy acceleration, a major card-level role change.

Both Supporters shuffle the user's hand into the deck and draw a fixed replacement hand. Lillie's Determination draws six instead of five, with a further increase to eight only when exactly six Prize cards remain.
Both Supporters shuffle the user's hand into the deck and draw a replacement hand. Judge draws four rather than five and also resets the opponent's hand, a material additional disruption effect.

Both are 70-HP single-prize Grass Basic Shaymin that support a team's Energy. The source moves already attached Energy through a Bench-triggered Ability and supplies spread healing, whereas the target must attack to search and accelerate one Energy to a Benched Grass Pokémon, preserving only the broad support slot.

Both Special Energy cards attach to Fighting Pokémon and provide Fighting Energy. The source boosts attack damage, while the target instead prevents non-damage effects of opposing attacks, preserving the Energy slot but substantially changing its secondary utility.

Both Supporters share the condition that one of the user's Pokémon was Knocked Out during the opponent's previous turn and then provide card recovery. Hassel selects up to three cards only from the top eight rather than searching the full deck for two, materially reducing precision.

Both are 130-HP single-prize Fire Basic Volcanion with matching Weakness and Retreat Cost and Fire-Energy interactions in their attacks. The source accelerates discarded Energy to the Bench, while the target burns or returns its attached Energy to the hand, a major strategic difference within the same Pokémon slot.

Both Items immediately return Pokémon from the discard pile to the hand. Night Stretcher returns only 1 rather than up to 2 Pokémon with 90 HP or less, while permitting any Pokémon and offering Basic Energy instead, a material quantity and eligibility tradeoff.

Night Stretcher exactly preserves Rescue Stretcher's immediate mode of returning 1 Pokémon from the discard pile to the hand. Its alternative recovers a Basic Energy instead of shuffling 3 Pokémon into the deck, so only the secondary mode changes.

Both Supporters search the deck simultaneously for a Pokémon, a Trainer-category card, and a Basic Energy. Larry's Skill narrows Trainer to Supporter and discards the user's hand instead of requiring a Knock Out on the prior turn, preserving the distinctive three-part search with a major timing and resource-cost change.

Both Supporters heal multiple Pokémon without a separate play condition. Fennel heals 40 from every Pokémon rather than 50 from up to 2 chosen Pokémon, retaining spread healing while changing both per-target amount and board-wide reach.

Both cards are unconditional Supporters that directly search the deck for Trainer cards. Petrel can retrieve either an Item or a Pokemon Tool and therefore preserves targeted Trainer access, but it returns only one card instead of Arven's simultaneous Item-plus-Tool pair; that material loss in search yield warrants confidence 2.
